description: KGS Learning Log. Active entries maintained by Process 3.8; acted-on entries archived weekly. The synthesis process reads the index for fast lookups and full entries for weekly review.
migrated_from: v1.0 Cross-Surface Performance Memory (Creative Intelligence §6.8A). v2.0 replaced rigid schema with flat learning log. v2.1 added index layer, consolidation, and bandwidth-aware reads.

config.domain_note: Free-text field. Recommended values: paid-media, content, lifecycle, website, campaigns, operations, cross-surface. Each department's instruction file defines which keywords it matches on — that's the authoritative routing, not this config.
config.synthesis_cadence: daily capture during pipeline run, weekly deep review Fridays
config.archive_policy: Process 3.8 archives acted-on entries weekly during Friday synthesis. Archived entries move to archived_entries array (preserved for audit). Active entries = un-acted + last 90 days acted.

entry_types._note: SINGLE CANON (2026-07-05 decision): these six keys are the exclusive entry_type enum, enforced by scripts/pm_validate.py I4 and imported by scripts/pm_write_gate.py. The gate's former extra values (pattern_observation, operational_signal, team_feedback, data_correction) are source_type values, not entry types.
entry_types.skill_update: Decision rules, evaluation frameworks, thresholds, confirmed patterns — destined for skill files via Process 3.8
entry_types.process_change: Operational changes to domain/dept instructions, data pulls, pipeline steps. Entries with changeset_candidate: true surface as ChangeSet proposals.
entry_types.threshold_calibration: Threshold tuning (e.g., CPL boundaries) — requires measurement before committing to skill file
entry_types.changeset_outcome: Auto-appended when any ChangeSet closes. Includes outcome_class (confirmed/minor_variance/significant_variance) and variance_pct for estimation calibration.
entry_types.content_pattern: Content performance pattern bridged from Moe's Performance Memory with cross-domain implications. Platform-specific hook weights stay in content-producer-skill.md §3.
entry_types.staleness_alert: Brain reference file past its staleness threshold (Amendment 10, written by scripts/check_brain_staleness.py). Cleared when the owner re-validates the file.

entries.learning: A scheduled task's proof-of-run has to be a side effect of the work itself, never an artifact the task is instructed to produce. When the evidence is something the prompt asks for, the failure that kills the task kills its evidence too, and the monitor cannot tell 'ran clean' from 'never ran' — silence reads as success. The repeatable move is to push the mechanism into code that executes as part of the work and leave only judgment in prose: pm_eval.py now writes its own I1 run record on --apply, so the record exists iff scoring ran and no SKILL.md has to remember anything.

entries.correction: MECHANISM CORRECTED 2026-08-04. L-299 states 'Only the per_date_* series honour the window.' They do not — they are all-time too, spanning 2025-11-13 to 2026-08-03, eight months before window_start. Every scalar total equals the EXACT all-time sum of its own per_date_* series (total_conversions 4,741 vs 4,741; total_posts 3,929 vs 3,929; total_impressions 94,345,796 vs 94,345,796) against 515/305/5,247,019 in the declared 30d window. confirmed_revenue has no dated counterpart at all, so it cannot be windowed in-file even in principle. The magnitude holds: $369,006.58 vs a true $47,762.47 = 7.73x. ROOT CAUSE is not the field alone but the SLIM VIEW: pipeline-data-contract dropped `conversions` (the canonical source named by metric-compute-map) and per_date_total_conversions from the content/lifecycle copy, while keeping insights_window_days:30, the all-time confirmed_revenue, and a _note describing a 30d array no longer present. entries.learning: pat-pmax-branded-inefficiency is an artifact of the pattern detector, not a property of the Google account. Its four instances are four DIFFERENT campaigns and three are not branded at all (CS-070 + CS-187 = pmax__shopping feed only; CS-136 = prospecting wedge A; only CS-240 = branded__pmax__troas). ZERO of the four was ever executed or validated: expired_unexecuted, expired_unexecuted, invalid_premise, invalid_premise. The common element is the string 'PMAX' beside a low weekly ROAS - a coincidence, not a mechanism. Synthesis 2026-07-29-s1 and 2026-07-31-s1 (rec-363) used the recurrence COUNT as corroborating weight; that inverts the evidence. Root cause: pattern_instance tags are free text minted at domain-scan time. task-a-scans.md:508 specifies L-NNN|pat-NNN|DS-NN (registry-backed IDs); this slug matches none, so nothing validates it, nothing resolves it to a definition, and no instance outcome is ever fed back. Any scan seeing a PMax campaign under-perform can re-mint it indefinitely. RULE: a recurrence count is not evidence when no instance was ever executed - check prior instances' OUTCOMES before citing a pattern as corroboration. Second-order lesson: branded__pmax__troas weekly ROAS ranges 1.11x-5.34x across five weeks (2.93x blended, clears the 2.0 floor 4 of 5 weeks), so NO single-week read of a PMax campaign in this account can support a de-prioritization decision, corrected basis or not.

Cannibalization unsupported: week ending 08-02 PMax spend $499.49 -> $263.72 while total branded conversions rose 60 -> 78 (both campaigns up) - a joint rise, not the trade zero-sum cannibalization predicts. entries.learning: Age-based ChangeSet expiry and the self-silencing L1/L2 focus-gap rule compose into a loop that neither mechanism can see. The shadow engine proposed expiring CS-2026-234 as expired_unexecuted; cross-referencing expected_impact.metrics_moved across all 56 active rows shows it is one of only TWO carriers of active_sub_count, an L2 lever 248 subscribers behind its 2,800 milestone. entries.learning: Provenance, not bundle width or reviewer capacity, is what produces expired_unreviewed ChangeSets. Pipeline-authored rows expire at 36% (42/117), human-requested at 6% (2/32) - a ~6x separation against ~2x on bundle width, with a majority of deaths single-surface. The quick subtype - cheapest to action - dies fastest of all three at 50%, which inverts the effort explanation and points at demand legitimacy.

entries.learning: A metric pair can be simultaneously in-band and blind. d12_velocity_new_per_week (12, top of [8,12]) counts rows ENTERING the pipeline and d12_stale_approved_count (3, favourable) counts rows sitting in approved, while all 44 expired_unreviewed deaths occurred strictly between those states, in draft. Second-order defect: stale_approved reads favourably partly because its denominator collapsed - 5 rows in approved against 20 in draft, so the metric improves when nothing reaches approved. Check state-transition coverage, not just band membership.
entries.evidence: Both metrics measure states, not transitions, and no metric covers the draft-to-approved transition where the failure lives. The absence of drift is itself the finding. See daily synthesis 2026-08-14-s1.md.

entries.learning: Engagement rate is inversely related to reach, so an unweighted per-post mean is the wrong baseline for an anomaly gate. Posts under 200 impressions average 5.49% ER while contributing 0.6% of weekly reach; posts over 5,000 average 2.00% but only 1.37% impression-weighted while carrying 78% of reach. Any >5x/<0.2x gate built on the unweighted 3.59% mean classifies every high-reach post as an anomaly - which alone explains two weeks of zero graduation candidates.
entries.source: dept-content 2026-08-14 INS-C-2, reach-banded decomposition of 875 posts

entries.learning: Google Search Console week-over-week comparison is directionally rigged, not merely noisy. The build reads an unsettled current window against a prior window that has had a full extra week to backfill. All 20 overlapping window pairs in the snapshot archive revise upward on re-read, median +23%, extremes +9.8% and +486% (one window went 819 to 4,801 clicks). No GSC decline in this dataset should be escalated at scan time, and no correction factor is honest at that variance - remove the field.

See daily synthesis 2026-08-14-s1.md.

archived_entries.learning: Department briefs overstate impact severity when research contradicts existing positioning — but the pipeline trusts those assertions verbatim for changeset generation. CS-2026-068 and CS-2026-077 were both rated CRITICAL based on the dept-science-research brief claiming three papers 'directly contradict current Kenetik claims.' Root cause: no validation step between brief severity assertion and changeset tier assignment.

Triggers: (a) same content format (e.g., 30-60s short-form video), (b) compatible message progression (hook → proof → positioning), (c) claims envelope accommodates all three, (d) trend windows overlap. archived_entries.learning: Paid ROAS rising while site CVR falls is an attribution ceiling, not a growth signal. Paid cannot create revenue above what the funnel can convert; reported ROAS lift in this state typically reflects (a) better-attributed existing demand, (b) pixel-platform divergence on specific creatives, or (c) audience shifting to higher-intent segments temporarily. Rule: when paid ROAS delta > 0 and site CVR delta < 0 for 2+ consecutive sessions, escalate to CVR-fix-before-spend-increase protocol. Amplifying spend on a broken funnel is negative-EV.

archived_entries.correction: MAGNITUDE REFUTED 2026-08-04. '~1/15th of real conversions' is not reproducible. The Superfiliate -> Shopify join is healthy: 570 of 578 finished conversions match an order (98.6%), and all 8 misses are same-day rows whose orders had not yet landed. End-to-end the real ratio is 248/578 = 42.9%, about 1/2.3. Two traced mechanisms account for it, and NEITHER is a logging failure: (1) attribute_day.py:1064 excludes confounded orders — is_amazon / is_draft / is_subscription_recurring, with Recharge renewals dominating at 37 of 72 orders on 8/2 — which is DELIBERATE, since a renewal is not creator-driven acquisition; (2) UTC/ET re-dating, because SF stamps UTC and the day bucket comes from Shopify's -04:00 timestamp. L-265's cited evidence date 7/8 logged 1 conversion and recomputes to 6 against today's files — a same-day freshness race. Every other day in the window reproduces its snapshot exactly, so the entry generalised a program-wide ratio from the single worst day in the series. OPEN AND ROUTED: whether the ~57% confound exclusion is a defect or correct behaviour is undocumented either way; until settled, creator conversion counts are not comparable to Superfiliate's raw count. The Polar limb is unverifiable from this repo — polar-state.json carries no creator dimension.

archived_entries.learning: BRIDGE AP-008: High-cadence reposting of identical workhorse copy collapses NCS. CP-002 ('He wakes up at 4am...') and CP-003 ('I was addicted to caffeine...') — the program's two most-validated FB hooks — each had identical text bodies published 14 times in 14 days. Every one of those 28 reposts scored NCS<5. Frequency, not the hook, is the failure mode. Cross-domain implications: (1) content scheduling must enforce a same-copy cooldown (≥7 days between identical text bodies on the same platform), (2) paid media amplification should not pair with same-week organic repost saturation, (3) campaign orchestration needs visibility into same-asset reuse cadence across organic + paid.

archived_entries.learning: BRIDGE AP-009: Large-reach ambassador 'awareness' posts deliver EMV but trivial revenue — high-EMV does not equal high-ROI. Reconfirmed across 4 independent weekly cycles, most recently (SYN-20260706) at its most extreme reading yet: JOSEPH 232,108 impressions / 1,335 unique visitors → 1 conversion / $33.75 revenue (0.07% visitor CVR) vs. BREAKTHROUGH 4,139 impressions → 23 conversions / $2,266.54 (6.0% CVR) in the same window — JOSEPH took ~56x the reach for ~1.5% of BREAKTHROUGH's revenue. Cross-domain implications unchanged and now higher-confidence: (1) creator selection should weight conversion fit over reach, (2) creator-ROI scoring needs a visitor-to-sale rate floor that triggers re-evaluation, (3) ambassador program review should surface awareness-only creators for repositioning or sunset. Moe's PM recommendation: weight conversions/revenue 10:1 over impressions/EMV in all ambassador ROI evaluation.
